**Pages:** elliptic-finite-difference-methods / elliptic-finite-difference-methods-examples.

**Scope:** On a rectangular uniform grid, define the five-point Dirichlet Laplacian and a divergence-form variable-coefficient flux stencil. source_record_verbatim.scope: Define SUPG for stationary convection-diffusion-reaction with explicit inflow/boundary conditions, tau_K scaling, diffusion epsilon>0, and c-div(b)/2 bounded below. source_record_verbatim.scope: Define single/double-layer potentials, boundary traces/jumps, Calderon operators and Galerkin BEM for 3D Laplace on a closed orientable Lipschitz polyhedral boundary. source_record_verbatim.scope: Define compressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier as a mathematical balance law with positive density/temperature, ideal-gas constitutive functions, nonnegative shear/bulk viscosity and heat conductivity, and specified periodic or entropy-compatible wall boundaries. Derive the continuous entropy identity for smooth positive states. Define a concrete mixed gradient/viscous DG or SBP flux discretization with entropy variables. Prove consistency, global conservation under periodic data and semidiscrete entropy dissipation under the stated positive-semidefinite viscous matrix and boundary flux. Define one finite fully discrete algorithm using the time agent's method; positivity and fully discrete entropy are separate theorems, and may require PE03 limiting plus a proved compatible time discretization. Prove a smooth-solution consistency/error estimate on a compact positive-state tube only when the exact discrete coercivity/linearized stability bound is proved. Sum local integration by parts, pair the gradient equation with viscous variables, and complete dissipative volume/face squares; compute wall entropy flux explicitly. Interpolate a smooth solution and derive the discrete error identity, controlling nonlinear coefficients by tube bounds, scheme coercivity and Gronwall. source_record_verbatim.title: First-order least-squares FEM and practical DPG
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define first-order-system least-squares Poisson on H(div)×H1_0 with residual `(sigma+grad u, div sigma-f)` and the correct norm. Prove residual norm equivalent to H(div)×H1_0 error and Galerkin best approximation; boundary conditions are encoded rather than omitted. Define ultraweak Poisson DPG on a stated simplicial mesh with skeleton H1/2 and H-1/2 quotient trace spaces, optimal trial-to-test map via the existing Riesz theorem, and a practical enriched broken test space. Prove continuous inf-sup, ideal energy best approximation, practical quasi-optimality and residual estimator equivalence using a concrete uniformly bounded Fortin operator for the chosen polynomial family/enrichment degree. State the exact degree enrichment from its proved construction. An arbitrary finite test space receives no stability claim.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: For least-squares recover grad u and sigma from the residual using weak Poisson energy, integration by parts and Poincare; triangle/divergence bounds give both inequalities. For ultraweak form define skeleton norms as minimum-energy extension norms, prove trace surjectivity and extension/lifting without consuming a C1-only boundary theorem on simplices. Prove injectivity/adjoint graph stability and BNB (NA34), then Riesz maps residual to optimal tests. Construct the practical Fortin map locally by moment constraints/bubble corrections, prove polynomial solvability/scaled norm bounds and face trace preservation, then transfer inf-sup. Computed QR/iterative algebraic residual and quadrature perturbations are separately bounded; normal equations still square the matrix condition number under the canonical theorem.

source_record_verbatim.title: Semi-Lagrangian characteristic transport
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define characteristic backtracking plus multilinear/barycentric interpolation for linear nonconservative transport on a periodic box or an explicitly resolved inflow/exit branch. Prove maximum/sup-norm stability for nonnegative partition-of-unity interpolation regardless of displacement-to-cell-size ratio. Prove a smooth-solution global error bound distinguishing characteristic foot error, interpolation defect per step and initial/boundary error: for fixed T, a typical bound is C(dt^q+h^(r+1)/dt) when each backtracking step has O(dt^(q+1)) foot error and interpolation has O(h^(r+1)) defect. State the actual joint mesh/time condition; absence of a classical advective CFL does not eliminate consistency constraints. Define a conservative characteristic-cell overlap method and prove mass conservation/positivity separately; pointwise interpolation is not inherently conservative. High-order interpolation receives its actual operator norm/limiter bound, not automatic L∞ contractivity.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Characteristic chain rule plus bounded velocity/state derivatives; prove backtracking map stays admissible and handle periodic wrapping/inflow first-hit. Existing ODE local error controls foot error via solution Lipschitz norm. Interpolation convexity proves sup stability; telescope one-step consistency defects with discrete Gronwall. For conservative remapping use Reynolds/Jacobian mass factors for divergence-form transport, orientation/invertibility and partitioned departure-cell measures, then PE17 overlap conservation. Boundary hitting error requires transversal events or exact exit oracle with declared error; no hidden root solve.

source_record_verbatim.title: Monotone Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman schemes and policy iteration
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define monotone upwind and positive-interpolation semi-Lagrangian schemes for a specified first-order HJ/HJB Cauchy problem, and a discounted stationary Bellman equation on a periodic domain with compact or finite controls and bounded Lipschitz coefficients. Prove monotonicity, L∞ stability, consistency and numerical-scheme-to-viscosity convergence by a full half-relaxed-limit argument using the exact existing first-order comparison class. A control minimization over infinite controls is an explicit oracle or a finite control discretization with its own uniform Hamiltonian error. Define finite-control Howard/policy iteration for the assembled proper M-matrix Bellman system; prove monotone improvement and finite termination with deterministic tie handling/no switch on equal value, or state a separately proved contraction stopping bound. Include a concrete second-order Bellman controlled-diffusion scheme on a monotone diagonal-dominant/wide-stencil branch; prove its comparison/convergence with new second-order viscosity suppliers. No generic central stencil monotonicity for arbitrary anisotropic diffusion, no unproved universal convergence rate.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Upwind/positive interpolation makes nodal update order preserving; positive discount gives stationary sup contraction and discrete comparison/unique solution. Finite policy matrices have verified M-matrix inverse positivity; compare successive value solutions, show each strict switch strictly improves at a component and eliminate repeated policies using tie rule, so finite policy space terminates. Derive consistency on smooth test functions including h²/dt interpolation and control-grid error where relevant. To pass numerical limits, choose strict touching test functions, extract near-maximal mesh nodes, apply discrete monotonicity replacing states by test-function values plus contact error, then take limsup/liminf; prove boundary/initial barriers and use continuous comparison to squeeze both limits. The published half-relaxed theorem applies to approximate PDE solutions, so this mesh-node consistency proof is genuinely new. For second order locally define semijets/degenerate ellipticity, prove the required theorem of sums via sup/inf convolution and twice-differentiability arguments (with actual local analytic suppliers), then doubling variables and discount produce comparison; prove Perron/barrier existence or obtain it from convergent discrete approximants. These large but established proofs belong here before their consumers, not a citation to Barles–Souganidis. Restrict a second-order theorem to the coefficient/boundary class for which all those estimates are supplied.
